meta.blog-epbd-iv-laadinfra.html.title: EPBD IV: mandatory charging infrastructure for hotels, what you need to know · Lemnion
meta.blog-epbd-iv-laadinfra.html.descrip: EPBD IV sets requirements for charging infrastructure at buildings with parking spaces from 29 May 2026. What does this mean for your hotel? All deadlines and requirements at a glance.
blog-epbd.h1: EPBD IV: mandatory charging infrastructure for hotels
blog-epbd.sub: What the new European buildings directive means for your parking area, and why investing now is smart.
blog-epbd.intro: The European Energy Performance of Buildings Directive (EPBD IV) came into force in the Netherlands on 29 May 2026. One of the most important parts for hospitality: charging infrastructure becomes mandatory at buildings with parking spaces. This is not some distant prospect · the first part already applies, and requirements for existing hotels follow from 1 January 2027.
blog-epbd.kort-li1: From 29 May 2026: requirements for new builds and major renovations with more than 5 parking spaces
blog-epbd.kort-li2: From 1 January 2027: existing hotels with more than 20 parking spaces must have at least 1 charge point per 10 parking spaces (or ducting for half of them)
blog-epbd.kort-li3: The requirements also apply to your own parking area outside the building
blog-epbd.kort-li4: Smart charging is explicitly encouraged. That is exactly what Lemnion focuses on
blog-epbd.p-nieuwbouw: For non-residential buildings, such as hotels, with more than 5 parking spaces:
blog-epbd.li6: Pre-cabling for 50% or more of the parking spaces (ducting for the rest)
blog-epbd.p-bestaand: Do you have an existing hotel with more than 20 parking spaces? Then from 2027 the following applies:
blog-epbd.li7: At least 1 charge point per 10 parking spaces, or
blog-epbd.li8: Ducting for half of the parking spaces
blog-epbd.p-2033: From 1 January 2033 stricter requirements follow (pre-cabling for half of the parking spaces, for government buildings).
blog-epbd.p-reken: A hotel with 30 parking spaces must have at least 3 charge points from 2027 (1 per 10). With a smart system · battery + EMS + load balancing · you can install those charge points without expensive grid reinforcement, even in a region with grid congestion.
blog-epbd.h2-betekent: What does this mean for your hotel?
blog-epbd.p-drie: Three things are important to know:
blog-epbd.li9: Grid congestion is not an exemption. Can't upgrade your connection? You must still provide facilities (ducting, pre-cabling) or use smart charging with load balancing.
blog-epbd.li10: Third parties may operate the points. The obligation is about presence, not about who runs the charge points. A charge point operator (CPO) can install and operate them · you remain the point of contact.
blog-epbd.li11: DC fast chargers count just the same. For the number of charge points it doesn't matter whether you choose AC or DC · you are free to choose what suits your guests.
blog-epbd.p-meer: Hotels that invest now in chargers with smart energy management, linked to battery storage, will not only be compliant later but also gain an advantage:
blog-epbd.li12: Operational advantage: charging during off-peak hours with stored energy, lower peak load, lower energy costs
blog-epbd.li13: Marketing advantage: EV charging becomes an expectation of guests · a hotel with chargers is more attractive
blog-epbd.li14: Revenue: every charged kWh can generate EREs (Emission Reduction Units), on top of the regular charging margin
blog-epbd.li15: Subsidies: SPRILA subsidises private charging infrastructure at companies · up to €3,900 per DC charge point (SME)
blog-epbd.td2: 1 charge point per 5 parking spaces + pre-cabling 50%
blog-epbd.td4: 1 charge point per 10 parking spaces or ducting for half (from 2027)
blog-epbd.bron: Source: RVO.nl, EPBD IV and RVO.nl, Laadinfrastructuur EPBD (checked July/August 2026).
